Technology. It's just unbelievable seeing everything that's happening, and you can even try to get involved in shaping it.

What we've already seen come to be:

  • The internet. Something which has completely reshaped and remodeled society, and will always be remembered.

  • The electric vehicle. Does anybody even remember about 15 years ago? The only option aside from gas were these hybrid cars which had the performance of a slightly glorified go-cart. It was mostly just hipsters virtue signaling to each other.

  • Solar energy as a thing. 20 years ago the most practical use of solar was charging a calculator. Today some homes can already be completely off-grid and decentralized.

  • Micro-scale computing. You can squeeze computers with more power than state of the art machines had 20 years ago into a watch today - and it costs in the tens of dollars.

  • Full rocket reuse. This has more relevance in the next section, but even by itself - can you believe there was a time when we used to simply throw away rockets that cost tens of millions of dollars to build once they flew once?

What is imminently coming:

  • Automation. This has been happening for decades - the average worker today has a productivity of about 250% higher than one in the 50s. But what I'm referring to is visible autonomous machines completely replacing humans. This will likely be the single greatest change in the entire history of humanity. For millenia we've relied on mass labor to keep society churning. In your lifetime this will change. And that in turn will have completely unpredictable revolutionary scale changes on everything.

  • Asteroid mining. Gold? Platinum? Silver? We highly value these things, but in reality they're incredibly abundant not even in the universe but in our very near solar system. 433 eros is an asteroid in our solar system that has more gold, vastly more, in it than has ever been mined in the entirety of Earth's history - all in a nice tidy body that's about 20 miles long. Oh yeah, we've also already landed on it. We just didn't have the technological level yet to completely destroy all scarcity of precious metals.

  • Interplanetary colonization. This is coming vastly faster than most realize. SpaceX first set a goal of the early 2030s. Given faster than expected progress that goal has been changed to 2024 for the first humans to depart Earth to set foot on Mars. And the goal there is not to get a research outpost or two - but genuine and real colonization. To try to create a parallel planet, eventually reaching self sustenance, developing independent of Earth. Again, the implications of this are impossible to even imagine. It's just almost surreal seeing things like Budweiser already taking steps to figure out how to become the first brewery on Mars. In related news, Mars travelers are encouraged to BYOB.

Overall

There's so many things going that it's a shame I can only pick a few, but it's really a bizarrely fortunate time to be alive. Many of the these things are not just once in a lifetime opportunities. All the things I mentioned as imminently coming are once in a species, once in a civilization, events - that people will look back on for the rest of the history of our species. The fact we have a front row seat to this show is something that I think lends even more credence to the simulation hypothesis. Whatever the reason, we're at a time that will almost undoubtedly be seen as one of the most relevant and huge turning points in the path of our species.
